title.narrative: SFCG: Engaging CSO in Eastern Congo Power of Civic Space - SFCG: Engaging CSO in Eastern Congo in Power of Civic Space

description.narrative:
Search For Common Ground (SFCG) har ansökt om finansiering på 44 995 758 SEK för att genomföra "Engaging CSO in Eastern Congo in Power of Civic Space program" under perioden 30 november 2020 till 31 december 2024.
Programmet syftar till att stärka förmågan hos flickor, kvinnor, pojkar och män som organiserar sig i det civila samhället att påverka samhällsutvecklingen. Därmed bidrar programmet till att främja demokrati, en mer inkluderande styrning på lokalnivå, jämställdhet och politiskt deltagande. Programmet kommer att genomföras på lokal nivå i den östra delen av landet.
Programmet kommer att: • Aktivera civilsamhällesorganisationer, varav flera leds av kvinnor och många bidrar till samhällsservicen, för att främja säkerhet, mänskliga rättigheter, styrning och fredsprocesser • Öka och effektivisera de primära intressenternas röster gentemot statliga institutioner • Inrätta och underlätta en samrådsprocess mellan medborgare och myndigheter på provinsiell, territoriell och lokal nivå så att de antar metoder och förfaranden som svarar mot medborgarnas krav på ansvarstagande, öppenhet, inkluderande styrning, respekt för jämställdhet mellan könen och skydd för medborgarna rättigheter; • Stärka organisationernas operativa och tekniska kapacitet, representativitet och nätverk; • Stärka organisationernas integrering av mänskliga rättigheter på olika nivåer.
SFCG kommer att genomföra programmet tillsammans med lokala organisationer i tre provinser i östra DRK, nämligen Nord-Kivu, Syd-Kivu och Tanganyika.
Insatsens totala budget är 44 995 758 SEK och Sida är den enda givaren till programmet.

The overall goal of the programme is to work to strengthen the capacity of civil society to promote democracy and to improve inclusive governance, gender equality, and women's and youths political participation in DRC. In doing so, it will seek the following outcomes:
Outcome 1: Strengthened civic and political participation of CSOs is characterized by increased responsiveness and accountability to conflict-affected communities in Eastern DRC, especially the most marginalized such as women and youth;
Outcome 2: Democracy for all is promoted through effective governance systems which allow conflict-affected communities to defend and enforce their rights, supported by responsive and accountable duty-bearers and power-holders;
Outcome 3: Peacebuilding and stabilization efforts allow conflict-affected communities to collectively negotiate and influence decision making, redress grievances, and resolve disputes through fair and inclusive local mechanisms, within a context of open civic space and respect for human rights.
Actions taken to accomplish these Outcomes include: Community-led research, such as actor mapping, conflict analysis, and participatory action research to identify barriers and opportunities; Skills trainings on capacity building, conflict resolution, and leadership for CSOs, activists, and authorities; Lobbying, advocacy, and communications campaigns to ensure responsive governance and research uptake among policymakers and governance structures.
The overall goal of this cost extension phase is to foster inclusive governance in South Kivu. This goal will be supported by three specific objectives:
Objective 1: Reinforce sustained civic engagement of civil society in South Kivu. Objective 2: Increase trust and collaboration on issues of governance and civic participation between civil society and local authorities in South Kivu. Objective 3: Promote civic norms that favor inclusive, accountable decision making and responsible engagement.
Across the above mentioned objectives, a particular emphasis will be put on addressing a range of technical (land governance and natural resource governance, decentralization) and cross-cutting issues (role of women, youth, and minorities in governance), which have been identified during the previous phase.
SFCG sees an opportunity to build upon the success of the first phase of Power of Civic Space with additional actions aimed at:
Reinforcing knowledge, skills, and networks to strengthen the capacity of civil society in South Kivu to effectively promote inclusive governance; fostering deeper collaboration with local authorities to actively embrace and support meaningful civic engagement; supporting efforts between communities and local authorities to jointly identify and address issues related to governance and civic engagement.
